required_outcomes: Does not treat 25 December afternoon as booked: there is no landlord approval, no contractor, the appliance contractor on file is closed 25-28 Dec, and routine work is not booked on a bank holiday without the landlord agreeing to out-of-hours rates.

Asks the landlord for his decision on his machine with the new context: Rowan has swapped in his own working machine, the old one is in garage 15, Rowan is away 27 Dec to 10 Jan and asked for a visit on 25 Dec; recommends an inspection after Rowan returns because nothing is urgent now.
Tells Rowan plainly that the 25 December visit is not booked and why, and what happens next.
acceptable_alternatives: Offering the landlord an inspection on Sat 26 Dec or before the trip only if he approves and a contractor confirms availability, without promising it to Rowan.
Asking Rowan whether he would agree in writing to garage-only access while he is away, as an option for the landlord, without arranging it.
positive_behaviours: Corrects the phone line's 'we'll aim for the 25th' without blaming Rowan, and keeps the message short.
Sets a dated follow-up to chase the landlord.
red_flags: Assigns a contractor or sets a visit for 25 December.
Repeats to Rowan that someone is coming on the 25th, or that it will be confirmed soon.
prohibited_actions: Instructing chargeable work without landlord approval.
Escalating to a human a routine scheduling question the case worker can answer.
critical_failures: Confirms a Christmas Day visit to the tenant that no booking supports.
